novel_features.name: Substitute finder
novel_features.description: Find current racquets whose specs match a target SKU within a tolerance band — head size, strung weight, swingweight, and exact string pattern.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-row similarity scoring over the local catalog. The Tennis Warehouse website has no "racquets similar to this one" surface.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When a player's racquet cracks or is discontinued, picking a replacement requires triangulating across 9 spec fields. This command does it in one call.

novel_features.name: Spec compare
novel_features.description: Render an aligned spec-by-spec table for 2–5 racquets with diff highlighting; --json emits a row-per-spec matrix.
novel_features.rationale: Pure local SQLite read over the racquet catalog. No web page joins the spec data for multiple racquets side-by-side.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Replaces opening 2–5 browser tabs and copy-pasting specs into a spreadsheet.

novel_features.name: Used-vs-new deals
novel_features.description: Find used listings whose price is a steep discount versus the new-racquet MSRP — joins used inventory against the new catalog.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-entity JOIN between used_listing and racquet MSRP. Tennis Warehouse exposes used and new on separate pages with no comparison view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Surfaces the actual bargain hunt — "40% off new for a Grade A unit" is the buy signal, not "$150 vs unknown."

novel_features.name: Price drop tracking
novel_features.description: List used listings whose latest price snapshot dropped below a prior snapshot beyond a threshold within a time window.
novel_features.rationale: Joins each used_listing to its price_snapshot history. Tennis Warehouse has no price-history view at all.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Catches deals the website cannot expose because it stores no historical pricing.

novel_features.name: New-arrival feed
novel_features.description: Used listings whose first_seen_at falls within a recent time window — "what is new since I last looked."
novel_features.rationale: SQLite query over a first_seen_at column the sync populates. The website has no "new since" view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Used inventory churns fast and good Grade A units sell in hours — the new-arrival feed is how bargain hunters actually shop.

novel_features.name: Inventory depth
novel_features.description: Aggregate per-physical-unit counts grouped by model and condition grade — answers "how many Grade A Blade 98s are in stock right now?"
novel_features.rationale: Aggregation over per-unit rows that the site only exposes one model at a time on the order page.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Depth is a buying-confidence signal. One unit at Grade A is a gamble; twelve units is a healthy market.

novel_features.name: Watchlist + drops
novel_features.description: Save SKUs to a local watchlist; view current state; combine with drops to alert on watched-only items.
novel_features.rationale: Local watchlist table joined against price_snapshot history. The site has no watchlist with price-history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets a player track a small set of candidates without manually refreshing pages.

novel_features.name: Grip-size availability
novel_features.description: Find used units in a specific grip size grouped by model and grade — wrong grip = unplayable, so this is a hard filter most shoppers care about.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-model grip-size aggregation. The web UI only shows grip per detail page.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Saves the shopper from clicking through every model to see if their grip size is even in stock.

narrative.headline: Every racquet Tennis Warehouse sells — new and used — searchable offline with spec compare, substitute finder, price-drop tracking, and grip-size availability no browser tab gives you.
narrative.value_prop: Tennis Warehouse has the deepest racquet catalog and used inventory in the U.S., but the web UI is browse-only and the data is locked behind page navigation. This CLI mirrors the entire catalog into a local SQLite store, then exposes the spec-driven and price-driven queries the website cannot answer — `racquets similar <sku>`, `racquets compare <sku> <sku>`, `used deals --min-discount-pct 40`, `used drops --since 7d`, `used new --since 7d`, `used depth --grade A`, `used watch <pcode>`, `used grip-availability --size 4_3/8`.
narrative.auth_narrative: No authentication required — Tennis Warehouse's catalog and used inventory are publicly browseable. Run `crawl` to populate the local store; everything else queries that store.

quickstart.comment: Populate the local SQLite store for Wilson — both new catalog and used inventory.
Filter the new catalog and emit only the fields an agent needs.

quickstart.command: tennis-warehouse-pp-cli racquets compare WB9810 WB9818 WB9816 --json
quickstart.comment: Diff three Wilson Blade 98 versions side-by-side.
Surface Grade A used listings selling 40%+ below new MSRP.
Watch a model and check for price drops since last sync.

troubleshoots.fix: The brand catalog path is `/{Brand}racquets.html` with capitalized brand. Verify the brand slug matches (wilson → Wilson, prokennex → ProKennex, head → Head).
Price drop detection requires at least two `crawl` runs separated by enough time for the site to update prices. Run `crawl` once, wait a day, crawl again.

troubleshoots.symptom: HTML parsing fails on a specific SKU
troubleshoots.fix: Tennis Warehouse occasionally redesigns individual product pages. Run `crawl <pcode> --debug` to dump the raw HTML and report the SKU in an issue.
Crawl is rate-limited to 1 req/sec by default with adaptive backoff. If you still see 429s, run `crawl --rate 0.5` to halve the rate.

narrative.when_to_use: Pick this CLI when you (or your agent) need to query the Tennis Warehouse catalog in a way the website itself doesn't support — spec-driven similarity, multi-racquet comparison, used-vs-new discount triage, or price-drop tracking. Use it for pre-purchase research, substitute-finder workflows after a discontinued frame cracks, or to drive a daily "new arrivals + drops" digest. Don't use it for placing orders, demos, or anything that requires a logged-in Tennis Warehouse account.

recipes.title: Find a substitute for a cracked racquet
recipes.explanation: Given your current racquet's SKU, returns the closest current models by spec — narrows a season-long replacement decision into one query.

recipes.title: Catch a Grade A bargain on a Wilson Blade 98
recipes.command: tennis-warehouse-pp-cli used deals --brand wilson --grade A --min-discount-pct 35 --json --select pcode,model,grade,price,msrp,discount_pct
recipes.explanation: Lists Grade A Wilson listings selling 35%+ off new MSRP — the joined-vs-MSRP view the website cannot show.

recipes.title: Compare three racquet generations side-by-side
recipes.command: tennis-warehouse-pp-cli racquets compare WB9810 WB9818 WB9816 --json
recipes.explanation: Aligned spec-by-spec table for Blade 98 v10, v8, and v9. Replaces three browser tabs.

recipes.title: Watch a model and check daily drops
recipes.explanation: Saves the SKU; lists every Grade A/B/C listing whose price dropped at least 5% in the last week.

recipes.title: Filter by grip size before anything else
recipes.explanation: Wrong grip is unplayable — start with grip, then narrow by brand/spec from there.
